segments.name: United States & Canada
segments.note: The biggest and richest market — 82.66M paid memberships after 2.53M net additions, with revenue per member of $17.30 a month, up 7% year over year.

segments.name: Europe, Middle East & Africa
segments.note: The second-largest region — 91.73M paid memberships after 2.92M net additions; revenue per member was $10.92 a month, flat year over year.

segments.name: Latin America
segments.note: 47.72M paid memberships after 1.72M net additions; revenue per member was $8.29 a month, down 4% as reported but up 16% on an F/X-neutral basis, reflecting price increases in Argentina and the peso's devaluation.

segments.name: Asia-Pacific
segments.note: 47.50M paid memberships after 2.16M net additions; revenue per member was $7.35 a month, down 8% year over year as reported, down 4% on an F/X-neutral basis.

takeaways.text: Netflix added 9.33M paid memberships, up from 1.75M a year ago, to end the quarter at 269.60M — paid memberships were up 16.0% year over year, with every region adding at least 1.7M members.
takeaways.title: Member growth surged

takeaways.text: Operating income rose 54% year over year to $2.6B on revenue growth of 15% — the operating margin reached 28.1%, seven points better than 21.0% a year ago, and net income rose 79% to $2.3B.
takeaways.title: Profit grew much faster than revenue

takeaways.text: Net income included a $131M non-cash unrealized gain from F/X remeasurement on Netflix's euro-denominated debt, recognised below operating income in interest and other income — a paper gain, not money from running the service.
takeaways.title: A paper currency gain helped profit

verdict: Netflix added 9.3M members and grew revenue 15% to $9.4B, and because costs grew far more slowly than sales, operating income jumped 54% to $2.6B and net income rose to $2.3B.
